bull_bear.body:
- Long-established brand in the Indian luggage industry - operating since 2001 and described as one of the top brands in India for strong, durable luggage
- Distribution reach: over 525 dealers across India plus over 300 dealers in France, giving both domestic and an overseas channel footprint
- Institutional / corporate gifting franchise built on long-term relationships with approximately 100 direct corporate clients across numerous sectors
- In-house manufacturing at Ahmedabad alongside the trading business, rather than a purely outsourced model
- Balanced product mix - hard luggage, office bags and backpacks account for about half of sales, with the remaining half in other products including a newly added ladies' handbag and purse segment
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Input cost volatility driven by global geopolitical upheavals — MD&A 'Risks & Concerns' names cost volatility from global geopolitical upheavals as a key identified risk that could adversely affect performance, future growth and cash flow; the Company relies on its ERM framework and internal controls to mitigate it.
- Import-related currency fluctuation exposure — MD&A explicitly flags import-related currency fluctuations among key identified risks - the Company buys inputs abroad and also has an overseas (France) presence, so rupee moves feed directly into landed cost.
- Intense market competition — MD&A names intense market competition as a key identified risk; the same bundle describes D2C and online-first brands restructuring the competitive landscape on pricing, product responsiveness and service, and forcing traditional retail-dependent brands to respond.
- Qualified audit opinion - GST records not made available for verification — Both the standalone and consolidated auditors qualified their opinion because the Company / Holding Company did not provide the GST electronic credit ledger, reconciliations and detailed GST payable workings, leaving the auditors unable to verify the related GST balances in the books of account.
- Qualified audit opinion - unpaid and unprovided direct-tax liabilities — The auditors report outstanding statutory liabilities under the Income Tax Act, 1961, non-filing of the Income Tax Return for AY 2025-26 and of applicable TDS returns for FY 2025-26 within prescribed timelines, and TDS liabilities still unpaid as at 31 March 2026. Management made no provision for interest, penalty or other liabilities that may crystallise, and disclosed no related contingent liability, so the auditors could not determine the consequential impact on the financial statements.
- Non-compliance with FEMA filing obligations for the French subsidiary — Directors' Report states that for Goblin France SARL the Company must file an Annual Performance Report (APR) and Return of Foreign Liabilities and Assets (FLA) with the RBI by 31st December and 15th July each year, but the APR and Form FLA for the relevant period were not filed.
- Compliance and disclosure control over related transactions — The Directors' Report records that, consequent to notice of a transaction (the underlying detail is not in the routed text), the Company initiated strict vigilance and an action plan requiring such information to be notified on a prior basis, indicating a lapse in prior intimation of that class of transaction.
- Dependence on a single manufacturing and headquarters location — MD&A states the headquarters and manufacturing plant are both based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, so operations, output and the automated capacity are concentrated at one site.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Established in 2001 and headquartered in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, where its manufacturing plant is also located, Goblin makes and sells travel gear - hard and soft luggage, backpacks, office and duffle bags, ladies' handbags and purses and travel accessories. It sells through a dealer network of over 525 dealers in India and over 300 in France, one Company-owned retail outlet in Ahmedabad, and B2B/B2C online channels. Alongside retail it runs an institutional business, catering to approximately 100 direct corporate clients and specialising in corporate gifting for brand promotion and brand reminders.

business.body:

- **Soft luggage:** Soft luggage, Duffle trolleys
- **Bags and backpacks:** Backpacks, Office bags, Duffle bags, Sling bags, Messenger bags
- **Ladies bags:** Ladies purses, Ladies handbags
- **Corporate gifting:** Customised corporate promotional / gifting products

- Institutional / corporate gifting franchise built on long-term relationships with approximately 100 direct corporate clients across numerous sectors
- In-house manufacturing at Ahmedabad alongside the trading business, rather than a purely outsourced model

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Scale automated manufacturing: management states current state-of-the-art automated machines have a production capacity of 1.2 million pieces and projects an anticipated annual production increase to 2.5 million pieces
- Stay a manufacturer-cum-trader across a diverse travel-gear range - luggage, duffle bags, laptop bags, casual bags, trolley luggage, chest bags and travel accessories - rather than a single-product player
- Compete on product innovation and technology: prioritise solving modern travel challenges with tech-savvy luggage and innovative designs
- Leverage manufacturing capability plus an extensive global network to deliver consistently high-quality products
- Seek new avenues of growth through the introduction of better and varied product lines and accessories (Board's Report)
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The only expansion the Company quantifies is manufacturing throughput: MD&A states that its state-of-the-art automated machines currently have a production capacity of 1.2 million pieces and that, with this technology in operation, it projects an anticipated annual production increase to 2.5 million pieces. No project name, commissioning date, phasing or rupee capex quantum is given for that step-up, and the routed bundle contains no capital-commitment or segment-capex disclosure. The rest of the bundle is third-party industry-outlook material on the Indian and global luggage market rather than Company expansion plans.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural growth in the Indian luggage market: cited at Rs. 17,000 crore (US$ 1.92 billion) in 2024 and projected to reach Rs. 26,700 crore (US$ 3.02 billion) by 2028 at a 12% CAGR (Motilal Oswal, cited by the Company)
- Formalisation of the category - branded players held a 52% market share in 2023 and are expected to outpace overall industry growth on urbanisation, premiumisation and product innovation
- Premiumisation: consumers increasingly treat luggage as a lifestyle accessory rather than a utility item, with shorter replacement cycles, particularly among Millennials and Gen Z; the premium category is the fastest-growing segment
- Smart / tech-enabled luggage (GPS tracking, USB charging, mobile connectivity) as an innovation driver, with the global smart luggage market cited as growing at 18.7% CAGR through 2030
- Continued expansion of e-commerce and modern retail formats, expected to further boost organised players; online sales cited at nearly 48% of global luggage purchases
- Shift in material and format preference from soft-sided to hard-shell polycarbonate and polypropylene, driven by cabin-size trolley demand and domestic air travel growth
- Widening demand base: rising domestic travel and disposable incomes plus a structurally expanding Tier-II and Tier-III buyer base
- Competitive pressure from D2C and online-first brands restructuring the competitive landscape on pricing, product responsiveness and service standards
- Board's Report notes operations improved during the current year compared with the decline in the previous year
